speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have presented with a breast mass; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have noticed this lump and if it is painful to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Given the rapid growth of the mass over four weeks, have you experienced any changes in your skin, such as dimpling, redness, or warmth? Also, have you noticed any discharge from the nipple or any swelling in your armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes tumor. The combination of a rapidly enlarging breast mass in a 48-year-old woman, lacking pain and skin/nipple changes, is highly suggestive of a phyllodes tumor rather than a typical fibroadenoma or carcinoma.
